architectureCatalog.name: MVC
architectureCatalog.description: Model-View-Controller pattern separating internal representations of information from user interface.
architectureCatalog.useCase: Monolithic web applications, simple to medium complexity CRUD systems.
architectureCatalog.dependencyRules: Views depend on Models; Controllers orchestrate Model and View interaction.

architectureCatalog.name: Repository + Service
architectureCatalog.description: Layered architecture separating data access logic (Repository) from business rules (Service) and transport (Controller/Handler).
architectureCatalog.useCase: Standard enterprise REST APIs and web services with moderate business logic.
architectureCatalog.dependencyRules: Upper layers depend on lower layer interfaces; data access is decoupled from controllers.

architectureCatalog.name: Clean Architecture
architectureCatalog.description: Hexagonal / Onion inspired architecture putting Domain Entities and Use Cases at the core with dependency inversion.
architectureCatalog.useCase: Complex domain logic, long-lifecycle systems needing framework independence and testability.
architectureCatalog.projectStructure: Domain -> Use Cases -> Interface Adapters -> Frameworks & Drivers
architectureCatalog.dependencyRules: Source code dependencies point inwards only. Domain entities know nothing of external systems.

architectureCatalog.name: Modular Monolith
architectureCatalog.description: Single deployable unit structured strictly into bounded modules with clear public APIs and isolated schemas.
architectureCatalog.useCase: Scaling development across multiple teams while avoiding premature microservices complexity.
architectureCatalog.dependencyRules: Modules only interact via public contracts/interfaces or asynchronous events.

rules.major: Dinaikkan jika membuat perubahan API yang tidak kompatibel ke belakang (breaking changes).
rules.minor: Dinaikkan jika menambahkan fitur baru yang tetap kompatibel ke belakang.
rules.patch: Dinaikkan jika membuat perbaikan bug atau patch keamanan yang kompatibel ke belakang.

zeroMajorRule.title: Tahap Awal Pengembangan Proyek (v0.y.z)
zeroMajorRule.description: Sesuai SemVer 2.0.0 (Klausul 4), versi Mayor nol (0.y.z) diperuntukkan bagi tahap awal pengembangan software. Versi dimulai dari v0.1.0-alpha.1. API publik belum dianggap stabil dan dapat berubah sewaktu-waktu sebelum rilis v1.0.0.

lifecycleStages.description: Tahap aktif pembuatan fitur awal sejak awal pembangunan struktur proyek (v0.1.0-alpha.1). Fitur mungkin belum lengkap, API bersifat eksperimental dan dapat berubah tanpa pemberitahuan sebelumnya, serta logging debug aktif.
bestPractices: Proyek baru dimulai dari v0.1.0-alpha.1 untuk modul atau prototipe pertama.
Dibuat secara otomatis oleh pipeline CI dari branch fitur aktif atau build harian.
Dibatasi ketat hanya untuk pengujian internal developer & QA; tidak boleh diekspos ke klien.
Perubahan breaking changes sepenuhnya diizinkan dalam revisi alpha.

lifecycleStages.audience: QA Engineer, Tester UAT, Pengguna Awal
lifecycleStages.description: Seluruh ruang lingkup fitur yang direncanakan telah selesai dibuat dan digabungkan (Feature Freeze). Fokus beralih ke pencarian bug, profiling performa, pengujian integrasi, dan umpan balik pengguna.
bestPractices: Feature Freeze diterapkan ketat: tidak ada penambahan fitur baru atau refactor besar.
Dideploy ke Staging / UAT untuk proses persetujuan dan verifikasi stakeholder.
Bug yang ditemukan diperbaiki dan dirilis dengan nomor tag beta berikutnya (misal v0.1.0-beta.2).

lifecycleStages.audience: Lead QA, DevOps, Auditor Keamanan, Product Owner
lifecycleStages.description: Build kandidat final yang diyakini telah siap masuk ke lingkungan produksi. Diuji menggunakan data riil tiruan produksi, pemindaian keamanan, dan simulasi beban kerja puncak sebelum dipromosikan.
bestPractices: Hanya perbaikan bug regresi kritis atau patch keamanan tingkat tinggi yang diizinkan.
Jika ada perubahan kode, nomor RC baru wajib di-tag (misal v0.1.0-rc.2).
Wajib mendapatkan persetujuan akhir (sign-off) dari Lead QA dan Product Owner sebelum rilis stabil.

lifecycleStages.description: Rilis resmi produksi yang telah lolos seluruh pengujian pada siklus RC. Menandai peralihan dari tahap pengembangan awal (v0.y.z) menuju garansi kompatibilitas ke belakang dan SLA produksi resmi (v1.0.0+).
bestPractices: v0.1.0 mendefinisikan baseline stabil internal untuk modul pertama yang selesai.
v1.0.0 mendefinisikan standar baseline API publik resmi untuk lingkungan produksi.
Di-tag langsung pada branch main / release setelah versi RC lolos seluruh kriteria.
Disertai dengan Catatan Rilis (Release Notes), Panduan Migrasi, dan Changelog otomatis.
Tag Git bersifat immutable (tidak boleh diubah atau ditimpa setelah di-push).

apiVersioning.deprecationPolicy: Provide a minimum 6-month deprecation notice before sunsetting old versions with 'Sunset' and 'Deprecation' HTTP headers.
guidelines: Never introduce breaking changes to existing versioned endpoints without bumping the major version.
Adding new optional fields to existing response payloads is backward-compatible and does not require version bump.
Maintain backward compatibility for at least 1 previous major version during migration windows.

branches.name: main / master
branches.purpose: Production-ready, thoroughly verified code. Direct pushes are strictly prohibited.
branches.protection: Branch protection enabled, code review required, automated CI checks must pass.

branches.name: staging / develop
branches.purpose: Integration branch for QA testing, staging verification, and pre-release acceptance.
branches.protection: Automated build & test CI checks must pass.

branches.name: feature/*
branches.purpose: Branch for developing specific features, branched from develop/main.

branches.name: fix/* / hotfix/*
branches.purpose: Branch for urgent bug fixes on production or staging environments.

branches.name: release/*
branches.purpose: Release preparation branch for final stabilization, version bumping, and changelog generation.

types.description: Changes that do not affect code meaning (formatting, whitespace)
Code change that neither fixes a bug nor adds a feature
Adding missing tests or correcting existing tests
Changes that affect the build system or external dependencies
Changes to CI/CD configuration files and scripts
Routine repository maintenance or auxiliary tooling changes

examples: fix(payment): resolve precision rounding in invoice calculation
docs(api): update swagger documentation for project endpoints

problemDetailsRFC7807.description: RFC 7807 Problem Details specification for standardizing machine-readable HTTP error payloads.

format.title: Resource Not Found
format.detail: Project with ID 42 could not be found.

httpStatusCodes.name: OK
httpStatusCodes.usage: Standard successful GET, PUT, PATCH request.

httpStatusCodes.name: No Content
httpStatusCodes.usage: Successful request with no response body (DELETE).

httpStatusCodes.name: Bad Request
httpStatusCodes.usage: Malformed JSON syntax, invalid query parameters, or business rule violation.

httpStatusCodes.name: Unauthorized
httpStatusCodes.usage: Authentication missing, invalid JWT, or expired token.

httpStatusCodes.name: Forbidden
httpStatusCodes.usage: Authenticated user lacks permissions / role to access the resource.

httpStatusCodes.name: Not Found
httpStatusCodes.usage: The requested entity or endpoint does not exist.

httpStatusCodes.name: Conflict
httpStatusCodes.usage: State conflict (duplicate unique key, concurrent edit conflict).

httpStatusCodes.name: Unprocessable Entity
httpStatusCodes.usage: Payload validation failed (invalid field formats, missing required fields).

httpStatusCodes.name: Internal Server Error
httpStatusCodes.usage: Unhandled exception on server (never expose stack traces in production).

httpStatusCodes.name: Bad Gateway
httpStatusCodes.usage: Upstream server or reverse proxy error.

rules: Catch all unhandled exceptions with a centralized global exception handler / middleware.
Always return consistent JSON envelope for both success and error responses.
Include traceId / correlationId in all error responses for instant log tracing.
Never leak stack traces, database credentials, or internal query text in production responses.
Validate all request inputs at the edge/controller layer before invoking business services.

testPyramid.scope: Fast, isolated tests validating individual functions, methods, domain logic, and validation rules using mocks for external dependencies.
Validating interactions between components (Controllers, Services, Repositories, Database, Caching, and Message Queues) using ephemeral databases / Testcontainers.
Validating end-to-end user workflows, critical UI journeys, and complete API transaction flows in a staging-like environment.

bestPractices: Follow Arrange-Act-Assert (AAA) or Given-When-Then test structure.
Keep tests deterministic, independent, and runnable in any order.
Avoid testing third-party library internals; test application domain contracts.
Execute unit and integration tests automatically on every Pull Request in CI.
Use test factories / builders (e.g. Bogus, FactoryBot) for realistic fixture data.

deploymentCatalog.name: Local Development
deploymentCatalog.description: Standardized local workstation environment setups for developers ensuring fast feedback loop and minimal setup friction.
deploymentCatalog.useCase: Day-to-day coding, unit testing, debugging, and feature development.
requirements: Docker Desktop / Colima for backing services (Postgres, MySQL, Redis)
deploymentCatalog.deploymentFlow: git clone ➔ copy .env.example to .env ➔ docker compose up -d (db, redis) ➔ run database migrations ➔ run local dev server
advantages: Instant hot reload and live debugging
disadvantages: Potential developer OS inconsistencies if dependencies are installed directly on host

deploymentCatalog.name: Docker
deploymentCatalog.description: Container platform providing lightweight virtualization to package applications and dependencies into standardized containers.
deploymentCatalog.useCase: Local development, reproducible testing environments, and standard deployment artifacts.
deploymentCatalog.deploymentFlow: Code ➔ Build Image ➔ Tag ➔ Push to Registry ➔ Run Container

deploymentCatalog.name: Docker Compose
deploymentCatalog.description: Multi-container orchestration tool for defining and running multi-container Docker applications via YAML specification.
deploymentCatalog.useCase: Small to medium self-hosted deployments, staging environments, developer local setups.
deploymentCatalog.deploymentFlow: Git Pull ➔ Configure .env ➔ docker compose up -d --build
disadvantages: Limited automated scaling and zero-downtime rolling updates compared to K8s

deploymentCatalog.name: VPS / Bare-Metal Deployment
deploymentCatalog.description: Deploying directly on Virtual Private Servers (VPS - e.g. Ubuntu / Debian / Windows Server) using systemd or Windows Service with Nginx / Caddy reverse proxy and Let's Encrypt SSL.
deploymentCatalog.useCase: Cost-effective production hosting for small-to-medium systems, enterprise on-premise servers, or dedicated infrastructure.
requirements: systemd unit file / Windows Service (sc / nssm)
deploymentCatalog.deploymentFlow: Provision VPS ➔ Setup User & Firewall (UFW) ➔ Deploy Binary/Code ➔ Configure systemd daemon ➔ Setup Nginx Reverse Proxy with SSL ➔ Enable auto-start on boot
advantages: Maximum raw hardware performance without virtualization overhead
Full root control over server resources and networking
Very low operational cost for standard workloads
disadvantages: Manual server patching and maintenance required
Host environment configuration drift if not automated with Ansible

deploymentCatalog.name: CI/CD Automation Pipeline
deploymentCatalog.description: Automated Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment workflows using GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or Jenkins. Optional for standalone VPS setups, highly recommended for team collaboration.
deploymentCatalog.useCase: Automating test suites, linting, build checks, and auto-deploying code on merge to main/staging branches.
requirements: Deployment Secrets (SSH Key / API Token / Webhook)
Server Runner or SSH Deploy Agent
deploymentCatalog.deploymentFlow: Git Push / PR ➔ Lint & Test Automation ➔ Build Artifact/Image ➔ (Optional on VPS) SSH Deploy / Webhook Trigger ➔ Health Check Verification
disadvantages: Optional complexity for single-server VPS setups where manual deploy or simple script suffices

deploymentCatalog.name: Windows Service
deploymentCatalog.description: Long-running executable applications that run in their own Windows session without requiring a logged-in user.
deploymentCatalog.useCase: On-premise enterprise Windows environments, legacy integration, local hardware daemon.
deploymentCatalog.deploymentFlow: Publish binary -> Register Service (sc create / nssm) -> Start Service

deploymentCatalog.name: Linux Service (systemd)
deploymentCatalog.description: System and service manager for Linux operating systems providing process supervision and logging.
deploymentCatalog.useCase: Bare-metal or VPS Linux deployments for compiled binaries (.NET Core) or PHP-FPM / Node daemons.
deploymentCatalog.deploymentFlow: Copy binary -> Write /etc/systemd/system/app.service -> systemctl daemon-reload -> systemctl enable --now app

levels.description: Most detailed diagnostic messages containing full payloads and step-by-step state.
Information useful during development and debugging sessions.
Normal operational events tracking general flow of application.
Unexpected events or degraded performance that did not stop execution.
Failures and exceptions that prevent standard operation of a specific request.
Severe failures requiring immediate system-wide attention or causing service outage.

frameworkImplementations.description: Structured JSON logging using Serilog with Enrichers, correlation tracking, and request logging middleware.
features: Structured log parameters (e.g., Log.Information("Project {ProjectId} created by {UserId}", id, userId))
Automated HTTP request lifecycle & duration logging via UseSerilogRequestLogging()
Sensitive data masking / PII sanitization in output sinks

frameworkImplementations.description: PSR-3 structured JSON logging integrated in Laravel with daily file rotation and context middleware.
features: Daily rotating log files with configurable retention window
Global Middleware context injection via Log::withContext()

frameworkImplementations.description: Enterprise structured JSON logger replacing NestJS default logger with contextual class tagging and interceptors.
features: Custom LoggerService replacement across dependency injection tree
Global LoggingInterceptor for request/response latency measurement
AsyncLocalStorage for request-scoped correlation ID propagation

frameworkImplementations.description: Ultra-fast JSON structured logger for Express.js with automatic HTTP request/response serialization.
features: Zero-overhead high-speed JSON serialization using Pino
Automatic HTTP request & response payload logger middleware
Built-in Correlation / Request ID generator per connection
Automatic header and parameter redaction (Authorization, Passwords)

pillars.description: Standardized /healthz (liveness) and /readyz (readiness) endpoints verifying application runtime, database connection, and dependent services.
Continuous telemetry measuring request throughput (RPS), error rates (5xx), latency percentiles (p50, p95, p99), and host CPU/memory consumption.
End-to-end request tracing across distributed services using OpenTelemetry and W3C TraceContext headers.
Real-time streaming and indexing of structured JSON logs into centralized log stores (Elasticsearch / Seq / Grafana Loki).
External heartbeat probes (Uptime Kuma, Better Uptime) continuously checking service uptime and TLS certificate expiration.

standardEndpoints.purpose: Liveness probe: verifies that the server process is alive and responsive.
Readiness probe: verifies database, cache, and queue connections before routing traffic.
Prometheus metric scraping endpoint exposing performance counters, gauges, and histograms.

tools.name: Prometheus
tools.description: Time-series database for scraping application and host metrics.

tools.name: Grafana
tools.description: Comprehensive dashboards for visualizing metrics, traces, and system health.

tools.name: OpenTelemetry (OTel)
tools.description: Vendor-neutral open standard for collecting and exporting traces and metrics.

tools.name: Uptime Kuma
tools.description: Self-hosted monitoring tool for HTTP, ping, and port uptime verification with alerts.

tools.name: Seq / ELK Stack
tools.description: Centralized search, filtering, and analysis for structured JSON logs.

alertingRules.condition: HTTP 5xx error rate > 5% for 3 consecutive minutes
alertingRules.action: Instant Slack/Telegram notification and on-call paging.

alertingRules.condition: Server CPU or Memory usage > 85% sustained for 10 minutes
alertingRules.action: Alert channel notification for resource scaling review.

alertingRules.condition: p95 API response latency > 1500ms for 5 minutes
SSL Certificate expiring in less than 14 days
alertingRules.action: Automated renewal check and warning notification.

authentication.name: JWT (JSON Web Token)
authentication.description: Stateless token authentication with signed claims, short expiration, and refresh token rotation.

authentication.name: OAuth 2.0
authentication.description: Industry-standard authorization framework enabling third-party and federated login.

authentication.name: OpenID Connect (OIDC)
authentication.description: Identity layer built on OAuth 2.0 for single sign-on (SSO) and user identity verification.

authorization.name: RBAC (Role-Based Access Control)
authorization.description: Permissions assigned to roles (Admin, Member, Viewer); users are assigned to roles.

authorization.name: Permission-Based (Fine-Grained)
authorization.description: Granular capability flags (e.g., project:create, user:delete) evaluated per request.

applicationSecurity.name: HTTPS Everywhere
applicationSecurity.description: Enforce TLS 1.3 encryption for all data in transit; redirect HTTP to HTTPS.

applicationSecurity.name: Password Hashing
applicationSecurity.description: Use modern adaptive hashing algorithms like Argon2id or Bcrypt with adequate work factors.

applicationSecurity.name: Input Validation & Sanitization
applicationSecurity.description: Strict schema validation (Zod, FluentValidation, Joi) on all client and API inputs.

applicationSecurity.name: CORS Policy
applicationSecurity.description: Explicit origin whitelisting; avoid wildcard `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` with credentials.

applicationSecurity.name: Rate Limiting
applicationSecurity.description: Protect public endpoints and authentication routes against brute-force and DDoS.

applicationSecurity.name: SQL Injection Prevention
applicationSecurity.description: Always use parameterized queries or trusted ORMs; never concatenate raw SQL strings.

applicationSecurity.name: XSS & CSRF Protection
applicationSecurity.description: Content Security Policy (CSP), HttpOnly + SameSite cookies, and output encoding.

rules: Never commit secrets, passwords, or connection strings into git repositories.
Use environment variables or cloud secret managers (HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault).
Rotate secrets and API keys periodically.
